key_headlines.title: Korea-US Form Mega AI Alliance to Counter China's Tech Rise
key_headlines.summary: South Korean tech giants including Samsung, SK, Hyundai Motor, and Naver signed major AI semiconductor and physical AI partnerships with US big tech companies at President Lee's AI Summit on July 24th. The alliance aims to leverage Korea's manufacturing capabilities and US technology expertise to compete against China's advancing AI sector.

key_headlines.title: Financial Authorities to Announce Housing Finance Measures Soon
key_headlines.summary: The Financial Services Commission plans to release comprehensive housing finance measures shortly, incorporating public opinions from President Lee's real estate policy debate. Measures will maintain total loan volume management while considering targeted easing policies, particularly regarding non-resident single-home purchases.

key_headlines.title: Government Solidifies Plan to Strengthen Taxes on Ultra-High-End and Non-Resident Single Homes
key_headlines.summary: President Lee formalized plans to strengthen property holding taxes on ultra-high-end and non-resident single homes during July 23rd's real estate policy national debate. The tax reform package will differentiate tax rates based on price, use, and region while providing relief for actual residents.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Plunges 5.7% on Middle East Tensions and Oil Price Surge
key_headlines.summary: Korean stock markets experienced a 'Black Friday' on July 24th with KOSPI dropping 5.72% to 6,690.62 and KOSDAQ falling 5.32% as Middle East geopolitical risks triggered massive foreign investor selling. Oil prices surged on conflict escalation concerns, raising inflation worries and triggering consecutive circuit breakers this week.

key_headlines.title: Trump Imposes 12.5% Tariff on Korea; Overproduction Concerns Remain
key_headlines.summary: President Trump confirmed a 12.5% tariff on Korea under forced labor provisions, affecting major Korean industries including semiconductors, automobiles, batteries, and steel. While key export products were exempted from additional overproduction tariffs, risks remain for battery manufacturers facing raw material cost pressures.

sections.Hot Economy News: The South Korean government is moving aggressively on multiple economic fronts, with President Lee's real estate policy debate on July 23rd catalyzing major policy announcements. Financial authorities plan housing finance measures targeting non-resident single-home purchases and ultra-high-end properties through differentiated tax structures. Simultaneously, Korea is positioning itself in the global AI competition through a mega alliance with US tech companies announced at the AI Summit, combining Korean manufacturing prowess with American technological leadership to counter China's advancement.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Russia's central bank cut its key rate to 14.0% for the tenth consecutive month, with GDP growth forecasts downwardly revised to 0.0-1.0% from 0.5-1.5% previously. South Korea maintained its oil price ceiling at current levels due to inflation pressures exceeding 3% and the Bank of Korea's rate hikes impacting consumer purchasing power. The EU granted South Korea an exemption to import Russian LNG from the Sakhalin project, opening annual import channels of 2 million tons despite broader sanctions against Russia.
sections.Financial Markets: Korean financial markets experienced severe volatility on July 24th amid Middle East tensions and surging oil prices, with KOSPI crashing 5.72% to 6,690.62 and KOSDAQ falling 5.32% in tandem circuit breaker activations. Foreign investors sold aggressively, dumping 5.7 trillion won as inflation concerns resurfaced; this marked the fifth consecutive trading day with circuit breaker triggers. The government accelerated implementation of leverage product deposit requirements, raising Samsung and SK Hynix single-stock leverage ETF minimum deposits to 30 million won starting July 31st to stabilize markets.
sections.Industry & Technology: Korea's major manufacturing sectors face 12.5% US tariffs under Trump's forced labor provisions, affecting semiconductors, automobiles, batteries, steel, shipbuilding, and machinery industries with combined overproduction concerns exceeding 301 trillion won. Battery manufacturers like LG Energy Solution face cost pressures as they source materials from China and other countries impacted by broader tariff frameworks. Steel demand is rising from AI data center and semiconductor fabrication plant construction projects, improving margins in steel reinforcement and plate products despite overall market uncertainty.
sections.Real Estate: The government confirmed plans to strengthen property holding taxes on ultra-high-end and non-resident single homes through differentiated taxation based on price, location, and purpose. Restrictions on jeonse (lease deposit) lending to non-resident single-home purchasers emerged as a key policy mechanism, as the President attributed rapid price increases to excessive and unsecured lending practices. Debate continues regarding redevelopment and reconstruction projects, with government data showing 230,000 housing unit increases possible from 790 sites in Seoul and Gyeonggi province, challenging skepticism about supply effectiveness.
sections.International Economy: Middle East escalation drove crude oil prices near $100 per barrel, raising US inflation expectations and triggering market speculation about Federal Reserve rate hikes with 80% probability priced into September 2026 FOMC decisions. Trump directed trade investigations into the EU's Google antitrust penalties under Section 301, threatening retaliatory tariffs against European companies including potential Korean e-commerce firms like Coupang. Trump imposed 12.5% tariffs on Korea, China, and Japan while exempting major export products; Korea was simultaneously designated as a currency monitoring target by the US Treasury for the second consecutive reporting period.
sections.AI & Economy: Korea launched a mega AI partnership with US tech firms featuring semiconductor, physical AI, and robotics collaborations with Samsung, SK, Hyundai Motor, and Naver participants; the alliance emphasized leveraging Korean manufacturing with American technology to counter Chinese AI advancement. Hyundai Engineering held seminars on North American nuclear and small modular reactor (SMR) opportunities, as AI-driven data center expansion dramatically increases power demand; SMR technology is gaining traction as a low-carbon power solution for big tech firms securing reliable electricity. Naver is launching its 'AI Factory' computing resource rental business to address cloud computing shortages impacting big tech companies unable to secure sufficient computational capacity for AI infrastructure expansion.
sections.Others: The government maintained petroleum price controls at current levels, warning that Middle East escalation could push oil prices beyond $140 per barrel in full conflict scenarios, directly threatening economic stability. US optical communications stocks are attracting investment attention as AI infrastructure bottlenecks shift from GPU production to data transmission speeds via fiber optic networks. President Lee met with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to discuss expanded AI investment and cooperation opportunities during US-South America visits, signaling government commitment to securing foreign AI company investment and technology partnerships.
